content.text: I've reviewed every candidate location: the grant of rights (§2, including restrictions §2.7), the Territory / Corio Market Segment definitions, shared resources (§13), trademarks (§6), miscellaneous (§14), termination (§11), pricing/revenue-sharing (Exhibit B) and the sales and marketing exhibit (Exhibit D). No covenant restricts Corio's business, products or purchasing.

input.quote: 13.6 Independent Development: Covenant not to Sue. Nothing in this Agreement will be construed to prohibit either parties' right to independently develop the Developments contemplated above.
input.rationale: The Agreement imposes no non-compete or field-of-use covenant on Corio (our party). The only restrictions binding Corio are ordinary licence-scope and IP-protection limits: §2.7 bars copying/reverse engineering of Commerce One's Software, §12 bars distribution of escrowed Source Code, and §6.1 bars post-term use of Commerce One's Trademarks — none restrict what businesses Corio may operate or what products it may buy, build or resell. The Territory (§1.11) and Corio Market Segment (§1.3) provisions merely define the scope of the licences granted to Corio; they do not prohibit Corio from serving other segments with other products, and §1.3 expressly lets Corio retain customers that grow or are acquired above the threshold. The licences are nonexclusive (§2.1–2.4), Exhibit D's sales and marketing cooperation is expressly "non-binding", and §13.6 affirmatively preserves each party's right to develop independently. This meets the preferred position; no redline is warranted.
